newsitem.title: UK: Highland says UK market tough, Europe mixed.
newsitem.headline: Highland says UK market tough, Europe mixed.

text.p: Whisky-maker Highland Distilleries Plc said on Tuesday its UK market remains very difficult, with sales volumes continuing to contract and conditions in Europe are mixed.

Chairman John Goodwin said in a statement accompanying the company's half-year results that its main blended whisky brand Famous Grouse has performed well in difficult conditions, raising its market share to 13.7 percent from 13.0 percent, despite 3.0 percent fall in shipments.

The company raised its pre-tax profit 12 percent for the half-year to February 28 to 24.9 million stg from 22.2 million in the same period last year and increased its dividend to 2.1p per share from 2.0p.
Highland said the rise in the value of the pound had adversely affected the results by around one million stg.

This is the first time that Highland is including malt whisky producer Macallan-Glenlivet for a full period. It said the unit made a profit of 5.0 million stg but this was balanced by the cost of financing the acquisition, which produced an interest bill of two million stg.
Highland said its leading single malt brand, The Macallan, had performed very strongly in its main U.S. market, while Highland Park has shown good performance in Europe as well as the UK.
Goodwin said the addition of The Macallan and the introduction of the deluxe sector Famous Grouse Gold Reserve meant the company is well positioned for further development.
